item.title: Nagoya Morning Culture and Ogura Toast: Breakfast, the Nagoya Way — Guide
item.description: Nagoya’s kissaten coffee-house culture runs deeper than anywhere in Japan, and its beloved institution is the ‘morning service’: order a coffee before around 11am and toast, boiled egg and often more arrive at little or no extra charge, a custom born in the city’s frugal merchant culture that turned cafes into the region’s living rooms. The essential order is ogura toast — thick-cut bread, butter and a generous pile of sweet ogura red-bean paste — a combination invented in Nagoya a century ago, served everywhere from creaking Showa-era kissaten to the hometown Komeda’s Coffee chain.
